items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Hidehiko. Hidehiko Matsumoto. And he was a tenor player

ctx.x: Six Joes. And there was, uh, the leader was a bass player named Shin Watanabe. He later on formed Watanabe Productions, the production [company]. If it weren‟t for that production [company], you couldn‟t have any television program, something like that. It really became… and he was a bass player, and he also died, but the tenor player was one of the best, actually, probably one of the two best tenor players, this one we used to call “Sleepy,” because he looked like he was sleeping all the time. It was Matsumoto ……
Then, 1953, the first live house, jazz club in Tokyo, and….
